name: config.snapshot
title: Hash and masked view of the applied configuration
summary: Not in the original command brief. Required because the extension must be able to detect drift after a Connector restart or an out-of-band edit: comparing hashes is cheap, and the masked config lets Diagnostics show what is actually running without ever exposing a credential.

appliedConfigHash.description: Lowercase sha256 of the config Core is running -- the identical quantity connector.status#/result/appliedConfigHash reports, spelled with the identical pattern, never a truncated or re-encoded form of it. drift: true is how a snapshot says that hash no longer matches what the extension believes was applied.

matchesExtensionHash.description: Null when the caller supplied no expectation. Computed by the Connector against the hash the extension sent, so a clock-skewed comparison cannot produce a false 'in sync'.

maskedConfig.description: Structurally identical to the applied Xray config with every secret field masked at the sink (docs/architecture/32). Field NAMES are preserved, values are not.

invariants: A grep of maskedConfig for any pinned secret value MUST find nothing; LIVE-10 asserts it against a real keystore entry.
